nodes.name: Pull Side A (HubSpot)
nodes.notes: Looks up an existing HubSpot contact by last-modified date — finds records the pipeline hasn't processed yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. nodes.notes: Searches Airtable's 'Requests' table by formula (={LastModified} > DATEADD(NOW(), -1, 'days')) for records the pipeline hasn't handled yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Diff the Two Systems
nodes.notes: Diffs two streams by key into 4 lanes: only-in-A, same, different, only-in-B — the heart of the sync.

nodes.name: Create Missing in Airtable
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Requests' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Count In-Sync Rows
nodes.notes: Collapses all items into a single summary item (for counts and run stats).

nodes.name: Apply Updates to Airtable
nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Requests' table, matched on requestId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Backfill into HubSpot
nodes.notes: Creates or updates a HubSpot contact by email — HubSpot is the CRM system of record for this pipeline. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: HubSpot private-app token. HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.

nodes.name: Gather Sync Results
nodes.notes: Rejoins 4 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Guard Non-Empty query
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Sort Requests Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

# Augment company profiles: HubSpot & Airtable

**Pattern:** Data Enrichment · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers research-assistant work end to end across HubSpot, Airtable and Slack.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Pull Side A (HubSpot)
3. Pull Side B (Airtable)
4. Diff the Two Systems
5. Create Missing in Airtable
6. Count In-Sync Rows
7. Apply Updates to Airtable
8. Backfill into HubSpot
9. Gather Sync Results
10. Guard Non-Empty query
11. Sort Requests Newest First
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Align Field Names
14. Tag Pipeline Metadata
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
17. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing research-assistant work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Pull Side A (HubSpot) → Pull Side B (Airtable) → Diff the Two Systems → Create Missing in Airtable → Count In-Sync Rows → Apply Updates to Airtable → Backfill into HubSpot → Gather Sync Results → Guard Non-Empty query → Sort Requests Newest First → Save Execution Metadata → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Airtable aligned by hand for research assistant
- Reconciling HubSpot against Airtable after the two quietly drifted apart
- Research assistant work where "Pull Side A (HubSpot)" is still a manual step before HubSpot
- Research assistant work that only reaches HubSpot on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Airtable in step for research assistant, without anyone re-typing a row
- Compares HubSpot against Airtable before writing, so only genuine differences land
- A failed HubSpot or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this research-assistant build
- Branches rejoin before HubSpot, so a research-assistant run reports once rather than 19 times
- Every research-assistant run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; HubSpot private-app token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Compare Datasets does the matching instead of hand-rolled join logic — one node produces four labeled lanes (only-in-A, matching, different, only-in-B), and each lane gets exactly the action it needs (create / count / update / backfill) instead of one generic 'sync' branch trying to cover every case.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Swap Side A or Side B for a third platform and rewire the merge-by-fields key.
2. Intentionally create a mismatch between the two systems and trace which lane it lands in.
3. Change mergeByFields to a different key and see how the diff results shift.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your research assistant process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole research-assistant payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
